Definition

Fix a **charge** $M\in\mathbb Z$ and let $W_N$ be the finite q-wedge spaces of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]]. For $r\le s$ define
the connecting map
$\varphi_{r,s}(u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r})
=u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r}\wedge u_{M-r}\wedge u_{M-r-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{M-s+1}$,
so that new entries are the consecutive ground tail
$u_{M-N},u_{M-N-1},\dots$ appended to a prefix of length $N$. The **charge-$M$
Fock space** is the algebraic direct limit $F^{(M)}:=\varinjlim_{N}W_N$ of the
finite wedge spaces along these maps; equivalently it is the quotient of the
eventually-vacuum tensor space by the local wedge kernels. Write
$|\lambda;M\rangle$ for the image of the normally ordered semi-infinite word
with entries $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ indexed by the positive parts of the
partition $\lambda$, so that the vacuum $\varnothing$ corresponds to
$u_M\wedge u_{M-1}\wedge u_{M-2}\wedge\cdots$.

The **Laurent, positive and integral charts** of $F^{(M)}$ are

$$F_A:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_0:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A_0\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_{\mathbb Z0}:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}\mathbb Z[q]\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}],\ A_0=\mathbb Z[q].$$

The **separated q-adic topology** on the full field space is the one induced by
the filtration $q^nF_0$, never by $q^nF_A=F_A$; a finite $A_0$-label component
completes to a $\mathbb Q[\![q]\!]$-lattice, and the full-field component completes
to $\mathbb Q((q))\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}F^{(M)}_\mu$ for the label-weight
pieces. Separately, the integral $\mathbb Z[q]$-chart completes to a
$\mathbb Z[\![q]\!]$-lattice; this completion is not identified with
$\mathbb Q((q))$ and is not asserted to carry a $\mathbb Q$-vector-space
topology.

the vacuum $P$-weight $\Omega_M$ is normalised by $\Omega_0=\Lambda_0$ and

$$\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-\Bigl(\frac{e\,t(t-1)}{2}+tr\Bigr)\delta.$$

$\Omega_M-\sum_{\text{cells}}\alpha_{c-r+M}$, its size $|\lambda|$ is a separate
grading, and the $d$-eigenvalue is $\Omega_M(d)$ minus the number of residue-$0$
cells; no periodicity $\Omega_M=\Omega_{M-e}+\delta$ is asserted.

Definition

Fix $e\ge2$ and keep all conventions of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]:
the Cartan datum, the space $V_{\mathrm{aff}}=\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q(q)u_m$
with $u_m=z^av_j$ ($m=j-ae$, $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$), the operators
$K_h,E_i,F_i$, the classical weights $\lambda_j=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}$, and the
fixed coproduct $\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h$,
$\Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$,
$\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$ of
[[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]].
Put $Q:=q^2$ and $c:=Q-1$, and let $Y_j$ denote the operator "multiply the $j$-th
tensor factor by $z$", so that $Y_j$ is invertible with
$Y_ju_m=u_{m-e}$ in the $j$-th slot and different $Y_j$ commute.

**The affine Hecke algebra $\tilde H_N$.** For $N\ge1$, $\tilde H_N$ is the
unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra with generators $S_1,\dots,S_{N-1}$ and invertible
$Y_1^{\pm1},\dots,Y_N^{\pm1}$ subject to

$$S_i^2=(Q-1)S_i+Q,\qquad S_iS_{i+1}S_i=S_{i+1}S_iS_{i+1},\qquad S_iS_j=S_jS_i\quad(|i-j|\ge2),$$

$$Y_iY_j=Y_jY_i,\qquad S_iY_j=Y_jS_i\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad S_iY_iS_i=QY_{i+1}.$$

The element $t_i:=-q^{-1}S_i$ then satisfies $(t_i-q)(t_i+q^{-1})=0$; for a
reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}\in S_N$ put $S_w:=S_{i_1}\cdots S_{i_k}$
and $A_N:=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$ (well defined by the braid relations).

**The two-vector operator and its extension.** On residue tensors
$v_j\otimes v_k$ ($j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$) set

$$S(v_j\otimes v_k)=\begin{cases}-q\,v_k\otimes v_j,&j<k,\\ -\,v_j\otimes v_j,&j=k,\\ -q\,v_k\otimes v_j+(Q-1)v_j\otimes v_k,&j>k.\end{cases}$$

For a Laurent monomial $f=Y_1^pY_2^q$ define, with $s(f):=Y_2^pY_1^q$ the
swap of the two loop variables,

$$S(f\,w):=s(f)\,S(w)+(1-Q)\,Y_2\,\frac{f-s(f)}{Y_1-Y_2}\,w\qquad(w\in V\otimes V),$$

and extend linearly; the quotient $(f-s(f))/(Y_1-Y_2)$ is a Laurent polynomial,
so $S$ is a well-defined linear endomorphism of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes V_{\mathrm{aff}}$.
On $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ the generator $S_i$ acts by this operator on
the tensor factors $i,i+1$ and $Y_j$ acts on the $j$-th factor as above; this
defines the **affine Hecke action**.

$q_i=q$ for all $i$. Choose once and for all the representatives
$j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ of the residues of $I$, so that $j=e$ represents the residue
$0$; all indices $j-1$, $j+1$ below are read in this representative range.

define $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear operators $K_h$ ($h\in P^\vee$), $E_i$, $F_i$
($i\in I$) on $V$ by

$$K_hv_j:=q^{\langle\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1},h\rangle}v_j,\qquad E_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}\,v_{j-1},\qquad F_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i}\,v_{j+1},$$

where $v_0:=v_e$ and $v_{e+1}:=v_1$ are read cyclically, and $\equiv$ refers to

$\lambda_j:=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}\in P$ and **residue** $j\in I$.

$E_i(z^av_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}z^{a+\delta_{i0}}v_{j-1}$ and
$F_i(z^av_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i}z^{a-\delta_{i0}}v_{j+1}$. We write
$\mathrm{wt}(u_m):=\lambda_j+a\delta\in P$ and $l(u_m):=ae-j=-m$; the

use the tensor rule $\otimes_+$

$$f_i(x\otimes y):=\begin{cases}f_ix\otimes y,&\varepsilon_i(x)\ge\varphi_i(y),\\x\otimes f_iy,&\varepsilon_i(x)<\varphi_i(y),\end{cases}\qquad e_i(x\otimes y):=\begin{cases}e_ix\otimes y,&\varepsilon_i(x)>\varphi_i(y),\\x\otimes e_iy,&\varepsilon_i(x)\le\varphi_i(y),\end{cases}$$
